Week 71 Appendix: The Week Erosion and Resistance Tied

Federal force against a senator, a blocked slush fund, and a president's finances entwined with contracts defined a week of near-perfect balance.

This week combined escalating foreign-policy chaos with domestic institutional strain across multiple fronts. Trump's erratic Iran negotiation—announced, disputed by Iranian state media, then reversed under pressure from Netanyahu and Republican hawks—illustrated policy incoherence layered atop AI-generated propaganda and Memorial Day attacks on Democrats. Simultaneously, sustained ICE crackdowns at Delaney Hall produced repeated use of chemical agents against protesters, journalists, and a sitting U.S. senator, alongside DHS officials publicly denying documented hunger strikes and abuse. Courts pushed back forcefully: judges blocked the $1.8 billion 'Anti-Weaponization Fund,' voided the Kennedy Center renaming, dismissed the Ábrego García prosecution as vindictive, and struck down Alabama's discriminatory map—yet the DOJ simultaneously shielded Bondi from oath-bound testimony on Epstein files and opened retaliatory investigations into Carroll, Piker, and Benjamin. Financial self-dealing (Dell contracts, Pentagon loans to Trump Jr.-linked firms, park-fee diversions, FDA reversals after donations) deepened alongside primary purges of Republican dissenters (Massie, Cassidy, Cornyn) and a president publicly stating indifference to midterm consequences.
